title: Hyperelastic constitutive model discovery with differentiable finite elements and structure-preserving neural networks
abstract: arXiv:2603.26517v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: The discovery of constitutive laws from experimentally accessible measurements is a central problem in nonlinear computational mechanics. Many data-driven constitutive identification approaches rely either on paired strain-stress data or on full-field displacement measurements, both of which are difficult to obtain in realistic three-dimensional settings. We present a differentiable finite element framework for the discovery of hyperelastic material laws from partial observations, including boundary-only displacement measurements and global reaction forces. The method embeds the nonlinear finite element equilibrium problem directly into the learning loop, so that candidate strain-energy densities are assessed through the deformation fields and reactions they induce. translated_title: 基于可微分有限元与结构保持神经网络的超弹性本构模型发现
translated_abstract: 从实验可获得的测量数据中发现本构规律是非线性计算力学中的一个核心问题。许多数据驱动的本构识别方法要么依赖于成对的应变-应力数据，要么依赖于全场位移测量，而这两者在现实的三维场景中都难以获取。我们提出了一个可微分有限元框架，用于从部分观测数据中发现超弹性材料规律，这些观测数据包括仅边界处的位移测量和整体反力。该方法将非线性有限元平衡问题直接嵌入学习循环中，使得候选应变能密度可以通过其诱导的变形场和反力来评估。这一表述将力学平衡作为约束条件加以强制执行，并允许损失函数仅在观测位置进行评估。为确保物理可容许性
tldr: 该论文提出一种将非线性有限元平衡问题直接嵌入学习循环的可微分有限元框架，结合结构保持神经网络，仅从边界位移和整体反力等部分观测数据中即可发现物理上合理的超弹性本构模型。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a differentiable finite element framework that embeds nonlinear equilibrium directly into the learning loop, using structure-preserving neural networks to discover physically admissible hyperelastic constitutive laws from partial observations such as boundary displacements and global reaction forces.
